To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rasch analysis of the EPDS- 10 suggests the presence of a two-dimensional structure and the EPDS-7 and EPDS-8 are both unidimensional scales with acceptable fit to the Rasch model.
the EPDS-7 and EPDS-8 are more psychometrically sound than the EPDS-1, and have the same cut points for case identification.

Rasch analysis of the EPDS- 10 showed that the scale was multidimensional, and that removal of items 7 and 9 resulted in a unidimensional eight item version, EPDS-8, that showed no DIF and good fit to the Rasch model, and that revised cut points for the EPDS 8 were identified to maintain the case-identification of the original scale.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a psychometrically robust post-natal depression measure.
the measurement properties of the EPDS.

the psychometric properties of the EPDS- 10, in particular the extent to which the items are ordered appropriately, the extent to which there is differential item functioning (DIF) and whether the scale measures a unidimensional concept.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the original 10 item version of the EPDS should not be used as a unidimensional measure of postnatal depression, and that a revised 8 item scale (EPDS 8) should be used instead.
the EPDS, when used in a clinical setting, is an adequate scale for the identification of post-natal depressive feelings, but not for the identification of anxiety.
the EPDS-7 and the EPDS-9 are the most appropriate cut points for the identification of depression in post-natal women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EPDS-7/8/9/10 scale is not unidimensional and the EPDS-9/10 scale has a ceiling effect and is not suitable to be used in the measurement of post-natal depressive feelings.
a revised eight-item EPDS-8, with a revised cut-point of 9, would be a more appropriate tool for measuring depression in a community sample.
the EPDS- 10 is not a unidimensional measure of depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a revised 8-item version of the EPDS is a more valid and reliable scale than the original EPDS-10 for measuring postnatal depression in women in the community.
the EPDS-9 is a better scale for measuring depressive feelings in post-natal women than the EPDS-4.
the 10-item EPDS does not measure a single latent trait.
